raw_response:
I've been working this land for 20 years. I know Quzhou's soil — heavy clay loam on the plain, tends to compact. My family depends on this farm but my son and daughter-in-law pull in some income off-farm too, so I'm not desperate, but I still need a good harvest.

The plan is the same rotation I've always run: winter wheat goes in October, I harvest it in June, then I plant summer maize right after on the same ground. The whole 10.1 mu works twice a year.

**Wheat:** I'll use Jimai 22 — it's been reliable here for years, good disease resistance, decent yield. I'll do a basal application of phosphorus and potassium at planting, then split my nitrogen — half at planting, half at jointing. I'll irrigate at sowing (dry autumn is normal here), again at jointing, at heading, and once more at grain filling if the spring is dry like last year. That's 4 times. I'll spray twice — once for weeds early on, and once for aphids and powdery mildew before heading. I'll rotary till before seeding.

**Maize:** Right after wheat harvest I'll plant Xianyu 335 — good heat tolerance, fills well in our short summer window. Maize gets most of its water from summer rain but I'll irrigate at planting if the ground is too dry, and again at tasseling if needed. I usually do 2 irrigations. I'll apply herbicide right after planting, then watch for corn borer around tasseling — one more spray if I see pressure. Rotary till after wheat straw is chopped.

My older neighbor stopped deep ploughing years ago and his yields dropped. I'll stick with rotary — it's what I know and my back can still handle it.
